For instance, taking $\alpha=\frac{\beta}{2}$ and $\gamma = \frac{2}{\beta^2}$ yields the inf-sup constant $\tilde{\beta}=\beta/4$.

issues.failure_explanation: The inf-sup test function $v_h=\Pi_d(v)$ has $\|v_h\|_{d,h}^2 \lesssim (1+\gamma)\|p_h\|^2_{L^2(\Omega_h)}$ because $v_h\cdot n\neq 0$ on the unfitted $\Gamma_u$ (only $(v-v_h)\cdot n$ is bounded, by trace/interpolation, with an $O(1)$ constant). Hence the inf-sup constant of $b_h$ in the $\|\cdot\|_{d,h}$ norm scales like $\gamma^{-1/2}$ and the Brezzi constant $\beta$ of $A_h$ decays with $\gamma$ (at least like $\gamma^{-1/2}$, typically $\gamma^{-1}$); the paper hides this since $\lesssim$ only tracks $h$ and cut dependence. The final step requires $\gamma\beta(\gamma)^2>1$ (e.g. $\gamma=2/\beta^2$), which cannot be enforced by enlarging $\gamma$ since $\gamma\beta(\gamma)^2$ is bounded (or tends to zero). Equivalently, the boundary term $(v_h\cdot n,p_h)_{\Gamma_u}$ is of size $C\|p_h\|^2$ with $C$ independent of $\gamma$, so it is not made small relative to $b_h(v_h,p_h)$ by any choice of $\gamma$. The proof therefore does not establish a positive $\tilde\beta$ for any $\gamma$ when $\Gamma_u\neq\emptyset$.

failure_location.quote: Choosing $\alpha < \beta$ and assuming $\gamma$ is sufficiently large so that $\left(\beta - \alpha -\frac{1}{4 \alpha \gamma}\right) > 0$, we obtain the discrete inf-sup condition for $\tilde A_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must track the gamma-dependence of the inf-sup constant of A_h and supply a different argument controlling $(v_h\cdot n,p_h)_{\Gamma_u}$ (e.g. a different test-function construction or a modified formulation/norm) that yields a uniform inf-sup constant for some admissible gamma.
issues.overall_effect: Discrete stability (and hence well-posedness and the a priori error estimate) of the method with weakly imposed flux boundary conditions ($\Gamma_u\neq\emptyset$, i.e. mixed or pure flux BCs) is unproven; the pure pressure case $\Gamma_u=\emptyset$ (where the boundary term vanishes) is unaffected, as is Theorem thm:pressure-robust-alt.
issues.title: Stability proof for mixed BC is circular in the penalty parameter: inf-sup constant of A_h degrades with gamma
issues.why_classification: The stability guarantee in the paper's central regime (unfitted flux/mixed boundary conditions) rests on a circular argument, and fixing it needs new proof architecture rather than a local adjustment.

issues.failure_explanation: The quasi-optimality bound gives $\|u_h-\Pi_d u\|_{d,h}\lesssim \|u-\Pi_d u\|_{d,h}+\dots$, and $\|u-\Pi_d u\|_{d,h}^2$ contains $\gamma h^{-1}\|(u-\Pi_d u)\cdot n\|^2_{L^2(\Gamma_u)}$. The only tool invoked, the cut-cell trace inequality (eq:cut-trace), yields $h^{-1}\|(u-\Pi_d u)\cdot n\|^2_{\Gamma_u}\lesssim \sum_T h^{-2}\|u-\Pi_d u\|_T^2+\|\nabla(u-\Pi_d u)\|_T^2 \lesssim h^{2r-2}\|u\|^2_{H^r}$, i.e. order $h^{r-1}$, not $h^{r}$ as claimed. This is not an artefact: for RT$_0$ ($r=1$) the boundary term $h^{-1/2}\|(u-\Pi_d u)\cdot n\|_{\Gamma_u}$ is $O(1)$, and even in the body-fitted case the facet approximation error gives $h^{r-1}$. Since the whole flux error (including the $L^2$ part) is bounded through this quantity, the proof only yields $h^{r-1}$ for the flux when $\Gamma_u\neq\emptyset$, contradicting the stated (and advertised) optimal rate.

failure_location.quote: {The interpolation estimates for $u$, $\dv{u}$ and $p$, together with the trace inequality for the boundary term in $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ and Assumption~\ref{as:extensions}, then prove the theorem.}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, either weaken the statement to order $h^{r-1}$ in the penalty-weighted norm (losing the advertised optimality), or supply a new argument (e.g. different penalty scaling or a separate estimate of the $L^2$ flux error not routed through the $h^{-1}$-weighted boundary term) proving the optimal $L^2$ rate.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal-order a priori error estimate for the flux with weakly imposed flux boundary conditions (mixed and pure flux BC regimes) is unsupported; the argument only proves a suboptimal rate (no convergence at all for lowest-order RT in the $\|\cdot\|_{d,h}$ norm). The pure pressure case and Theorem thm:pressure-robust-alt are unaffected.
issues.title: Error estimate loses one order through the $\gamma h^{-1}$ boundary penalty term when $\Gamma_u\neq\emptyset$
issues.why_classification: An advertised optimal convergence rate materially worsens (by a full order) in the main regime of the paper, and no source-supported argument restores it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We assume that $u$, $p$ and $\dv{u}$ admit extensions to $\domext$, still denoted by the same symbols, such that $u \in [H^r(\domext)]^d$, $p \in H^t(\domext)$ and $\dv{u} \in H^s(\domext)$
where, for the last term, we have used the commutativity property $\dv{\Iv(u)}=\Iq(\dv{u})$ together with the weak consistency of $\shpf$ applied to $\dv{u}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption as:extensions provides separate extensions of $u$ (in $H^r$) and of $\dv u$ (in $H^s$) with no compatibility requirement. The proofs use $\dv \tilde u = -\tilde g$ on $\Omega^{ext}$ (pressure-robust theorem) and apply weak consistency in $H^s(\Omega^{ext})$ to $\dv\tilde u$ (error theorem). In general the divergence of an $H^r$ extension of $u$ is only in $H^{r-1}$ and need not equal the chosen $H^s$ extension of $\dv u$; for RT spaces $s=k_p+1=k_u+1=r$ is allowed, so the needed regularity $\dv\tilde u\in H^{s}$ with the stability bound is not guaranteed by the assumption as stated.

failure_location.quote: Since $\Iv$ commutes with the divergence on $\domext$ and $\dv{u}=-\tilde g$ in $\domext$, we obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption as:extensions to require a single extension $\tilde u$ with $\tilde u\in H^r(\Omega^{ext})$ and $\dv\tilde u\in H^s(\Omega^{ext})$ satisfying both stability bounds (such compatible extensions can be constructed, e.g. via a Bogovskii-type correction in $\Omega^{ext}\setminus\Omega$), and set $\tilde g\doteq-\dv\tilde u$.
issues.overall_effect: The divergence-correction identity $\dv w_h=-\pi_h^0(g)$ and the rate $h^s\|\dv u\|_{H^s}$ in both error theorems rely on an unstated compatibility of the extensions.
issues.title: Extension of $\dv u$ is assumed to coincide with the divergence of the extension of $u$ without hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard compatibility condition to the assumption leaves all statements, rates and proofs intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $k_u, k_p \in \{0,1,\ldots\}$ be the largest values such that $[\mathbb{P}_{k_u}(T)]^d \subset \V(T)$ and $\mathbb{P}_{k_p}(T) \subset \Q(T)$ for all $T \in \mathcal{T}_h$, respectively.
follows from a Taylor expansion argument for polynomial functions around points on connecting facets

issues.failure_explanation: The Taylor-expansion argument for $\|r_h\|^2_{L^2(\Omega_h)}\lesssim\|r_h\|^2_{L^2(\Omega)}+s(r_h,r_h)$ requires jumps of all derivatives up to the actual polynomial degree of the local space, but the sums in (eq:shface) stop at $k_u$, $k_p$, defined as the largest full-polynomial degrees contained. For $\mathbb{RT}_k$ the components have degree $k+1>k_u=k$. Counterexample for $\mathbb{RT}_0$ in 2D: let $T_2$ be a cut cell whose only active neighbour $T_1$ (interior) shares a vertical facet $F$ at $x=x_F$; take $u_h=(b(x-x_F),0)$ on $T_2$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then $u_h\in V_h$, $[u_h]_F=0$, so $s^d(u_h,u_h)=0$ and $\|u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ is arbitrarily small while $\|u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_h)}\simeq |b|h^2$; (eq:stab-assump-1) fails. Analogously $\mathbb{Q}_k$ pressures have mixed derivatives of order $>k_p$ not penalised.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the upper summation limits in (eq:shface) by the maximal polynomial degree of the local spaces $\V(T)$ and $\Q(T)$ (e.g. $k_u+1$ for $\mathbb{RT}_{k}$, $d\,k_p$ for $\mathbb{Q}_{k_p}$), and note that the weak-consistency argument (high-order terms via inverse inequalities) goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:enhanced-stability-FGP is false as stated for the Raviart–Thomas (and $\mathbb{Q}_k$) spaces the paper explicitly admits and uses in the FGP experiments; the abstract stability/error theory then does not apply to the face-based method for these spaces.
issues.title: Face-based ghost penalty with jumps only up to degree $k_u$ ($k_p$) fails to control RT/$\mathbb{Q}_k$ spaces
issues.why_classification: A local change of the summation range restores the lemma and all guarantees without altering the method's structure, rates or scope.
